> The operational examples assume that the SSPICE project root is the working directory. They are displayed but not run when the vignette is built because they require project data.

# From routing metadata to a graph

`build_DAG()` reads the routing metadata and produces the canonical DAG. With `stop_on_cycle = TRUE`, construction stops if dependencies are cyclic; `analyze = TRUE` computes structural diagnostics. The project script also saves the adjacency matrix, the transpose of the incidence matrix, numeric routing, and graph partitions.

```{r build-dag}
source(file.path("scripts", "00_config.R"))
dag <- SSPICE::build_DAG(
  routing = config$routing_file,
  separator = config$metadata_separator,
  na_strings = config$missing_codes,
  analyze = TRUE,
  stop_on_cycle = TRUE,
  max_paths_per_partition = config$max_paths_per_partition
)
names(dag)
dag$graph_diagnostics
```

# Interpreting the graph

Nodes represent variables and logical groups; edges represent routing prerequisites. Inspect source nodes, isolated nodes, partitions, and path lengths before attributing routing anomalies to the data. OR and XOR groups are represented by canonical VOR and VXOR variables. Acyclicity allows dependencies to be evaluated in a consistent order.

```{r inspect-dag}
source(file.path("scripts", "01_build_DAG.R"))
dag <- readRDS(file.path(config$dag_output_dir, "questionnaire_DAG.rds"))
str(dag$graph_diagnostics, max.level = 1)
utils::head(dag$routes_numeric)
```

If graph construction fails, correct the metadata and rebuild the DAG before reusing derived outputs. Step 09 separately generates the extended DAG with logical-edit nodes.
